name: Evidence summary: Shortlist molecular identities from tandem mass spectra
description: Plain-language summary of what the reviewed evidence shows. Draft until reviewed.

attributes.value: MSAlign ranks first among the formula-free methods on every split recorded, but its top-1 recall falls from about half on the formula split to under a fifth on the MCES split. On the MassSpecGym formula split, Recall@1 was 47.5 for MSAlign and 58.2 with score fusion, against 42.7 for Emb-Cos, 13.9 for JESTR and 4.7 for DeepSet, with standard deviations of 0.5 to 3.4 over three random splitting seeds. On the MCES split the order is the same but the values are much lower: 19.0, 30.8, 12.6, 7.9 and 1.9; the table caption describes three splits there too, but the methods describe two swapped variants. Recall@20 reaches 87.0 for MSAlign and 92.8 with score fusion on the formula split, and 64.9 and 82.0 on MCES. An earlier version of the same paper reports Recall@1 of 53.8 for MSAlign and 41.2 for Emb-Cos on the formula split, so the two versions differ and are not independent measurements. Every value assumes the true structure is among 256 mass-matched candidates, which is not open-world identification, and all of them come from two versions of one arXiv preprint, scored by the authors of the leading method.

name: Evidence summary: Select perturbations for a defined cellular response
description: Plain-language summary of what the reviewed evidence shows. Draft until reviewed.

attributes.value: No original submission scored far from what a random ordering would give on the challenge's own prospective score. Across the 20 original Challenge 2 submissions, the top-k overlap AUC ran from 0.452 to 0.566, and 17 of the 20 fell between 0.50 and 0.57; a random ordering is expected to score 0.5 on this curve. That score is the area under a top-k overlap curve, not a ROC AUC, and the genes it scores were drawn from the leading Challenge 1 nominations rather than sampled across the genome, which narrows what it measures. In the prospective follow-up, two nominated targets exceeded the Screen 1 targets on the immune checkpoint blockade objective. The source gives no denominator for that count: it reports 61 nominations, 57 selected targets, 59 screen-2 genes and 50 perturbations passing quality control in different places without reconciling them, so no success fraction follows. All values are author reported from one 2026 preprint, in T cells from a mouse melanoma model, with no uncertainty printed and no matched-budget random or conventional comparison.

name: Evidence summary: Compare methods for plant promoter experiments
description: Plain-language summary of what the reviewed evidence shows. Draft until reviewed.

attributes.value: AgroNT scored above the task-specific CNN in all six assay-by-species comparisons, but by 0.02 to 0.05 R-squared, with no uncertainty reported. On STARR-seq core-promoter strength, AgroNT reached R-squared 0.62 to 0.75 and the CNN from Jores et al. 0.57 to 0.73, across maize protoplasts and tobacco leaves for Arabidopsis thaliana, Sorghum bicolor and Zea mays sequences. In the earlier Jores study, which pools the three species, the CNN reached a squared Pearson correlation of 0.67 in maize protoplasts and 0.71 in tobacco leaves, against 0.45 and 0.51 for a GC and motif linear model. In an independent benchmark, five DNA foundation models separate Arabidopsis TATA and non-TATA promoter sequences from similar non-promoter sequences at AUC 0.937 to 0.961, but that is sequence classification, not reporter strength, and it uses a different dataset. The AgroNT and Jores values are reported by the authors of those studies, the six AgroNT comparisons all come from one figure of the AgroNT paper, and no value has a confidence interval or run variability. Nothing here covers stable transformed plants, tissue specificity or newly designed promoters.

name: Evidence summary: Assess rhodopsin wavelength prediction across sequence backgrounds
description: Plain-language summary of what the reviewed evidence shows. Draft until reviewed.

attributes.value: RhoMax, which adds structural binding-pocket inputs, had the lowest wavelength error on each of its own wild-type holdout splits. In separate Rewire runs on the FLIP2 split, two amino-acid composition probes outranked two frozen ESM-2 probes, and both ESM-2 probes fell below a constant control. Averaged over four RhoMax splits, mean absolute error was 10.45 nm for RhoMax, 13.46 nm for RhoMax plus retinal and 14.90 nm for the BLASSO comparator, with standard deviations of 10.9 to 11.7 nm; per-split RhoMax error ran from 7.28 to 16.68 nm. In electronvolts the three methods are closer, and on split 3 all three print the same mean absolute error of 0.045 eV. On the FLIP2 Rhomax by_wild_type split of 184 held-out sequences, Rewire's runs gave a Spearman correlation of 0.418 for a 40-feature amino-acid composition probe and 0.418 for a 22-feature one, against -0.146 for a frozen ESM-2 8M probe and -0.222 for a 35M probe; NDCG was 0.955, 0.955, 0.896 and 0.907 against 0.921 for a training-mean control, whose Spearman is undefined. The two split definitions are different and their scores must not be pooled. The RhoMax values are reported by its authors with no independent reproduction, and the Rewire runs are single runs with no seed variability, with the 35M checkpoint chosen after the 8M outcome was known.

name: Evidence summary: Set baselines for UTR translation experiments
description: Plain-language summary of what the reviewed evidence shows. Draft until reviewed.

attributes.value: Only two sequence-only controls have been measured on the target split, both in Rewire's own runs, so there is no model comparison on it yet. On the 15,003 held-out records of the mRNABench designed-reporter test split, the composition ridge control reached a mean squared error of 1.914 against 2.366 for the training-mean control, and a Pearson correlation of 0.437; the training-mean control has no defined correlation, because its prediction is constant. The published FramePool panels are the only model comparison recorded here: neural models (FramePool and Optimus) reached Pearson 0.743 to 0.966 on the two random-sequence panels and 0.700 to 0.894 on the two human panels, while k-mer random forests, which were evaluated on the random panels only, reached 0.616 to 0.877. Those values are reported in the FramePool study on its own library, one split per panel with no uncertainty interval, and they are not measured on the designed-reporter split, so they are not baselines for it. Both Rewire controls are single runs on one split with no seed variability, and their automated audit checks the run itself, not a published score.
